जटायुस्: Jaṭāyus, Jaṭāyu m.: A mythical vul-ture (गृध्र). A. Birth: Very strong (वीर्यवन्त्, महाबल) son of Aruṇa from his wife Śyenī; brother of Sampāti 1. 60. 67; 3. 263. 1. B. Status: Chief or king of vultures (गृध्रराज) 3. 263. 1, 6, 17; 3. 266. 49; (गृध्रपति) 3. 266. 49. C. Huge shape: Looked like a mountain 3. 263. 15, or a mountain peak 3. 263. 6. D. Association; Friend of Daśaratha 3. 263. 1, 17, 21; hence interested in the welfare of Rāma (राम-प्रियहितैषिन्) 3. 263. 5; hence also referred to Sītā as his daughter-in-law (स्नुषा) 3. 263. 2, (वधू) 3. 263. 3. E. Help to Rāma: From a mountain top he saw Rāvaṇa abduct-ing Sītā 3. 262. 41; he saw her on Rāvaṇa's lap; flew up to Rāvaṇa and asked him to release Sītā; when Rāvaṇa did not oblige, he attacked Rāvaṇa with nails, wings, and beak and wounded him severely; Rāvaṇa cut off his ‘arms’ (भुजौ) (that is wings) with sword 3. 263. 2-5; when Rāma saw Jaṭāyu he mis-took him for a demon; Jaṭāyu told Rāma who he was and about the abduction of Sītā; he also told that he was wounded on account of Sītā 1. 263. 16-19; F. End: When asked in which direction Rāvaṇa escaped Jaṭāyu could ‘tell’ only with the movement of his head, and he died; Rāma knew Jaṭāyu meant south; Rāma cremated him with due rites 3. 263. 15-21; 3. 258. 2; Sampāti, Jaṭāyu's brother, surprised when he heard Hanūmant and others talking about Jaṭāyu; Sampāti told them that his wings were burnt, but not of Jaṭāyus, when he and Jaṭāyus, in a competition, went to the assembly of the sun (आदित्यसंसद्); Hanūmant informed Sampāti about Jaṭāyu's death 3. 266. 45-53.
जनमेजय: Janamejaya m.: A mythical serpent. One of the serpents who, without feeling fatigue, wait on Varuṇa in his सभा; marked with a banner (पताकिन्), and round spots (मण्डलिन्), hooded (फणवन्त्) 2. 9. 10-11.
जय: Jaya1 m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 16, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7. [See Jaya2]
Jaya2 m.: A mythical serpent. Vāsuki gave two snakes, Jaya and Mahā-jaya, to the son of Agni (i. e. Skanda) 9. 44. 48. [See Jaya1]

Jaya m.: Name of a type of Itihāsa (जयो नामेतिहासो ऽयम्) 1. 56. 19; 5. 134. 17; 18. 5. 39. Usually this is considered to be the desi-gnation of that text which was originally composed by Vyāsa and later, with gradual additions, grew to become the Bhārata and the Mahābhārata at the hands of Vaiśāṃpāyana and Sūta Ugraśravas respectively; as the name of the Mahābhārata it probably occurs in the opening मङ्गल श्लोक found at the begin-ning of the different पर्वन्स् (नारायणं नमस्कृत्य नरं चैव नरोत्तमम् । देवीं सरस्वतीं चैव ततो जयम् उदीर-येत् ॥ ) which is not found in all the versions; according to V. S. Sukthankar, however, “ … Jaya is a गेनेरिच् name applicable to different works, and not a specific name of the Mahābhārata at all as believed by some writers” (Ādiparvan, p. 989, note on 56. 19); the recitation of this kind of Itihāsa should be heard by a king who desires victory; he then conquers the earth and shall defeat his enemies; it should also often be heard by a chief queen since it is as good as a rite calculated to lead to the birth of a son (पुं-सवनम्) and by a crown prince since it is the royal road to welfare (स्वस्त्ययनं महत्) 1. 56. 19-20; its recitation is re-commended for a king desiring prosperity (भूतिम्), for princes in general, and for any pregnant woman; it is also said that hearing it one who desires heaven will go to heaven, one who wants victory will win victory, and a pregnant woman will deliver a son or a fortunate girl (पुत्रं कन्यां वा बहुभागिनीम्) 18. 5. 39-40; the narrative called the Vidurāputrānuśāsana (5. 131-135) is also classed as the Jaya type of Itihāsa 5. 134. 17; a minister should recite this to a king who is oppressed by his enemies and who is dejected since this tract, being a powerful exhortation, is best suited to cause increase in energy (इदम् उद्ध-रणं भीमं तेजोवर्धनम् उत्तमम्); the rest of the श्रवणफल given here is the same as for the Mahābhārata (as a Jaya type of composition) with the addition which gives the qualities of the son to be born to a woman 5. 134. 16-21.

Jaya m.: Name of a मुहूर्त। Drupada asked his Purohita, whom he dispatched as his दूत to the Kauravas, to start for Hāstinpura at the time of the con-junction of the moon with Puṣya नक्षत्र and under the मुहूर्त Jaya (स भवान् पुष्ययोगेन मुहूर्तेन जयेन च । कौर-वेयान् प्रयात्व् आशु) 5. 6. 17.
जरत्कारु: Jaratkāru f.: A female serpent (भु-जङ्गमा) 1. 43. 18, 22, 27, 28; 1. 44. 12; 1. 49. 1; (भुजगोत्तमा) 1. 48. 25. A. Family: Younger sister (अनुजा स्वसा) of Vāsuki 1. 13. 34. B. Marriage: She was to be given in marriage to sage Jarat-kāru as alms (भैक्षवत्) when he came begging (for a girl of his name); this was originally the suggestion made by Brahmā to gods for saving serpents and it was reported to Vāsuki by Elāpatra 1. 34. 9-18; 1. 49. 13; this was told again by Brahmā to Vāsuki 1. 35. 8-11; so Vāsuki kept Jaratkāru without marrying her to any one 1. 13. 34; 1. 35. 2; when sage Jaratkāru announced his decision to marry a girl of his name, Vāsuki was informed of it by his serpent attendants; Vāsuki adorned his sister, told the sage that she had the same name as his, and assured him to maintain her even after marriage; sage Jaratkāru agreed to marry her; she was given as alms (भैक्षवत्) and with due rites 1. 42. 14-20; 1. 43. 1-4; 1. 13. 30-34, 36-37. C. Dutiful wife: The sage lived with his wife at the residence of Vāsuki; she agreed to her husband's condition (समय) not to do anything that would displease him and that if she did he would leave her; 1. 43. 7-9; once when she had bathed after her period she lay with her husband and conceived a child 1. 43. 11-12; after a few days when the sage had slept with his head on Jaratkāru's lap the sun was about to set; Jaratkāru awakened her husband for the evening rites; the angered sage got ready to leave her as his wife had displeased him; she told him that she woke him up not out of dis-regard but to save him from violating धर्म। D. Concern for kinsmen: She pleaded with the sage not to leave her until she bore him a son as she was anxious for the welfare of her kinsmen; the child she had already conceived might not be a son (अव्यक्तरूपं गर्भम् 1. 43. 36); the sage thereupon assured his wife that she would give birth to a fire-like, learned son 1. 43. 13-39; Jaratkāru informed her brother Vāsuki about the sudden departure of her husband; Vāsuki was scared but Jarat-kāru told him about the assurance her husband gave her and that he had never told a lie be-fore 1. 44. 1-13. E. Birth of Āstīka: Vāsuki honoured his pregnant sister in all ways, and at proper time Jaratkāru gave birth to a child of divine lustre (देवगर्भाभ) 1. 44. 15-17; he was named Āstīka 1. 44. 20; 1. 13. 37. F. Snake sacrifice: Vāsuki, terrified at the destruction of snakes in the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya, went to Jaratkāru and reminded her of the purpose for which she was married to sage Jaratkāru; he asked her to tell her son Āstīka to intervene and stop the snake sacrifice 1. 48. 20-26; Jarat-kāru informed Āstīka why she was married to his father and asked him to stop the sacrifice 1. 49. 1-16; Āstīka assured Jarat-kāru that he would fulfil the purpose of his birth 1. 49. 17; on completing his mission Āstīka informed his mother (and Vāsuki) what had happened at the snake sacrifice 1. 53. 17. G. Reward: Since Jaratkāru saved the life of snakes her name appeared in the मन्त्र to be recited for obtaining protection from serpents 1. 53. 22.
जरिता: Jaritā f.: A female शार्ङ्ग bird (शार्ङ्गिका, शार्ङ्गी 1. 220. 16; 1. 222. 16). Lived in the Khāṇḍava forest 1. 220. 19; sage Mandapāla turned himself into a शार्ङ्ग bird and became united with Jaritā; he begot on her four sons 1. 220. 16-17; when Mandapāla left his sons, still in the form of eggs, and went to Lapitā, another शार्ङ्ग female, Jaritā was very much worried out of her affection for the young ones 1. 220. 17-18; she did not aban-don the eggs and when they were hatched, she reared them as a bird would do (स्ववृत्या) 1. 220. 19; when the Khāṇḍava forest was on fire she was distressed and lamented for her sons who had then not developed feathers, or feet; she did not have strength enough to fly to a safe place taking all the young ones with her; she did not know whom to abandon and whom not; she therefore told her children that she would cover them under her wings and die with them 1. 221. 1-7; but the young ones suggested to her to abandon them and save her-self from fire 1. 221. 12; she then advised them to enter the hole of a mouse under a tree which she would cover with earth; when the fire sub-sided she would return and remove the earth 1. 221. 15-17; the young ones hesitated for the fear of the mouse; Jaritā tried to remove the fear by telling them that the mouse had been already picked up by a hawk (श्येन); the young ones were still sceptical; she once again told them that when the hawk took the mouse she flew behind the hawk and blessed him to be golden when he went to heaven for he had taken off the enemy of the birds 1. 222. 5-8; the young birds remained firm in their resolve not to enter the hole and asked their mother to fly away to a safe place; Jaritā then left her sons to their fate and flew away 1. 222. 10-16; when the fire had moved away from that place Jaritā, coveting her sons, returned and seeing them safe tears came to her eyes again and again; she could not believe that they were safe 1. 224. 17-19; Mandapāla also remembered Jaritā and his sons and wondered what might have happened to them in the fire 1. 224. 3-5; Lapitā, the other शार्ङ्गिका, en-vious of Jaritā asked Mandapāla to go to her for whom he was in anguish 1. 224. 11-13; Mandapāla met Jaritā and his sons, but the sons would not talk to him; Jaritā, too, asked Mandapāla what business he had with the young birds and told him to return to the young and sweet smiling Lapitā 1. 224. 21-25; Mandapāla blamed Jaritā for her distrust 1. 224. 26-31, but also acknowledged her being conversant with धर्म (धर्मज्ञता) 1. 225. 2; when all were reconciled Manda-pāla took his wife (भार्या) Jaritā and the sons with him and left for another country 1. 225. 4.
जरितारि: Jaritāri m.: A young शार्ङ्ग bird (शार्ङ्गक 1. 221. 1; 1. 223. 6; शार्ङ्ग 1. 222. 17-18). Eldest son of sage Mandapāla (turned into शार्ङ्ग bird) and शार्ङ्गी Jaritā; as the eldest son, he was considered by his father to be the mainstay of the family (जरितारौ कुलं हीदं ज्येष्ठोत्वेन प्रतिष्ठितम्) 1. 221. 8, 9; at the time of the Khāṇḍava fire he and his brothers advised their mother to abandon them and fly to a safe place 1. 222. 4, 10-14; they in turn were advised by their mother to enter the hole of a mouse but they hesitated 1. 221. 18-21; 1. 222. 2-4, 10-12; they preferred to enter fire, but if saved would be united with their mother 1. 222. 15; when the fire drew near Jaritāri addressed himself to his younger brothers and told them how an in-telligent person behaved in hour of difficulty 1. 223. 1-2; he folded his hands and on behalf of all of them praised god Agni who was burning the Khāṇḍava 1. 222. 18; 1. 223. 7-8; when all the brothers in turn had praised Agni, the god informed them that he had already agreed to their father's request to spare them 1. 223. 22; they were seen by their mother safe from the fire 1. 224. 18-19; when Mandapāla returned to them they did not greet him, nor spoke to him 1. 224. 20-23; later all were reconciled to their father (1. 224. 32) and went with him and their mother to a different country (1. 225. 4); all brothers described as ‘sages’ (ऋषि) and ‘knowers of ब्रह्मन्’ 1. 224. 8; 1. 225. 3; as ‘full of lustre’ (तेजस्विन्) and ‘heroic’ (वीर्यवन्त्) 1. 224. 8; 1. 225. 2; as ‘able speakers’ (समर्थास् ते च वक्तारः) 1. 224. 10.
जाम्बवत्: Jāmbavant m.: King of bears (ऋक्षराज 3. 264. 23; ऋक्षाधिपति 3. 268. 24). One of the four councillors (सचिव) of Sugrīva; intelligent and very strong 3. 264. 23-24; he came to help Rāma (रामकारणात्) with a hundred crores of bears 3. 267. 8-9; Lakṣmaṇa, led by Vibhīṣaṇa and Jāmbavant, crashed into the southern gate of Laṅkā 3. 268. 24; he was among those who applied water, sent by Kubera, to the eyes to enable them to see invisible beings 3. 273. 13; he and other monkey-chiefs with their armies sur-rounded Rāvaṇa when he came out of Laṅkā to attack Rāma 3. 274. 3; besides being king of bears, he is also called chief of the apes (कपीन्द्र) 13. 14. 24, and chief of the Vidyādharas (विद्याधरेन्द्र) 13. 14. 25.
जाम्बवन्त्: Jāmbavant m.: King of bears (ऋक्षराज 3. 264. 23; ऋक्षाधिपति 3. 268. 24). One of the four councillors (सचिव) of Sugrīva; intelligent and very strong 3. 264. 23-24; he came to help Rāma (रामकारणात्) with a hundred crores of bears 3. 267. 8-9; Lakṣmaṇa, led by Vibhīṣaṇa and Jāmbavant, crashed into the southern gate of Laṅkā 3. 268. 24; he was among those who applied water, sent by Kubera, to the eyes to enable them to see invisible beings 3. 273. 13; he and other monkey-chiefs with their armies sur-rounded Rāvaṇa when he came out of Laṅkā to attack Rāma 3. 274. 3; besides being king of bears, he is also called chief of the apes (कपीन्द्र) 13. 14. 24, and chief of the Vidyādharas (विद्याधरेन्द्र) 13. 14. 25.
जाम्बवती: Jāmbavatī f.: A female bear. Daughter of the bear-king Jāmbavant (कपीन्द्रपुत्री 13. 14. 24), one of the wives of Kṛṣṇa, mother of Sāmba; also called the daughter of the king of the Vidyādharas 13. 14. 25; described as सुमध्यमा (13. 14. 19) and called देवी (13. 14. 19; 16. 8. 71); twelve years after Pradyumna had killed Śambara and after seeing the eight sons of Rukmiṇī, Jāmbavatī approached Kṛṣṇa and requested him to bless her quickly with a son, heroic, handsome, and equal of himself (आत्म-तुल्यं मम सुतं प्रयच्छाच्युत मा चिरम्) 13. 14. 12-14; the son was to be strong and of agreeable valour (चारुविक्रम) like the sons of Rukmiṇī 13. 14. 18; Kṛṣṇa agreed to her request; she then permitted Kṛṣṇa to go to propitiate Śiva for this purpose 13. 14. 19; at the time of Kṛṣṇa's departure she pronoun-ced benediction (स्वस्त्ययन) on him for his safety 13. 14. 20-24; (Śiva granted Sāmba to Kṛṣṇa as his son 13. 16. 5); after the death of Kṛṣṇa she (with other three co-wives) entered the fire 16. 8. 71.
ज्योतिक: Jyotika m.: A mythical serpent. One of the sons of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 13, 2.
ज्योतिष्क: Jyotiṣka m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 15, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7.

Jyotiṣka nt.: Name of a summit of the mountain Meru. Described as famous in the three worlds (त्रैलोक्यविश्रुत); adorned with all kinds of jewels (सर्वरत्नविभूषित); immeasur-able and unassailable in all the worlds (अप्रमेयम् अनाधृष्यं सर्वलोकेषु) 12. 274. 5; the wind which blew there was auspicious, pleasing, carrying different fra-grances and pure (ववौ शिवः सुखो वायुर् नानागन्धवहः शुचिः), and the big trees there blossomed with flowers of all seasons (सर्वर्तुकुसुमोपेताः पुष्पवन्तो महा-द्रुमाः) 12. 274. 11; it was sacred to Savitṛ (सावित्र) 12. 274. 5; god (Śiva) once sat there (गिरितटे) with his wife and was attended by gods and other celestial beings 12. 274. 6-12.
जैत्र: Jaitra m.: Name (?) of Indra's chariot. The excellent chariot of Indra (स्यन्द-नोत्तम, रथोदार) Jaitra (? or ‘victori-ous’), drawn by bay horses (हर्यश्वयुज्), riding which Indra killed hundreds of Daityas and Dānavas; it was sent by Indra to Rāma while the latter was engaged in a battle with Rāvaṇa 3. 274. 13-14. [See Sudarśana2]
ज्योतिष: Jyotiṣa nt.: Name of a missile. Employed by Arjuna to dispel the dark-ness created by the माया of Śakuni 7. 29. 24, 15.
जटासुरवध: Jaṭāsuravadha m.: Name of the 34th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 44, 33, 70. Referred to while detailing the contents of the Āraṇyakaparvan 1. 2. 111; related to the incidents narrated in the अध्याय 3. 154.
जतुगृहस्य: Jatugṛhasya dāhaḥ: Name of the 8th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha (दाहो जतुगृहस्यात्र) 1. 2. 35. Alluded to, though not directly by this name, in the list of contents of the Ādipar-van 1. 2. 83; also listed by Vaiśaṃpāyana in his very brief enumeration of the main incidents for Janamejaya 1. 55. 16-18; related to the incidents narrated in the अध्यायस् 1. 124(? 129)-138.
जन्तूपाख्यान: Jantūpākhyāna nt.: Name of a narra-tive occurring in the Āraṇyakaparvan 1. 2. 119. In this narrative it is told that king Somaka sacrificed his son (Jantu) and got a hundred sons 1. 2. 119; the narrative occurs in the अध्यायस् 3. 127-128.
जम्बूखण्डविनिर्माण: Jambūkhaṇḍavinirmāṇa nt.: Name of the 61st पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 55, 33, 70. Referred to as an item in the list of the contents of the Bhīṣmaparvan 1. 2. 154; related to the अध्यायास् 6. 1-11.
जयद्रथवध: Jayadrathavadha m.: Name of the 69th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 57, 33, 70. Referred to in the list of the contents of the Droṇaparvan 1. 2. 163; the incident is included by Dhṛtarāṣṭra in his summary of the chief events made for Saṃjaya 1. 1. 135-140; related to the incidents narrated in the अध्यायस् 7. 61-121.
जरासन्धवध: Jarāsandhavadha m.: Name of the 22nd पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 40, 33, 70. Listed in the contents of the Sabhāparvan 1. 2. 98, (99); referred to by Sūta in his summary of the events made for the sages as-sembled in the Naimiṣa forest 1. 1. 86; related to the incidents narrated in the अध्यायस् 2. 18-22.
जलप्रदानिक: Jalapradānika nt.: Name of the 80th पर्वन् in list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 61, 33, 70. Alluded to in the contents of the Sau-ptikaparvan (?) 1. 2. 187 (तोयकर्मणि सर्वेषां राज्ञाम् उदकदानिके); related to the अध्याय 11. 27.
ज्येष्ठा: Jyeṣṭhā f.: Name of a constellation, also called Aindra (1. 114. 4; 6. 3. 15). A. Epic event related to this नक्षत्र: Kuntī gave birth to Yudhiṣṭhira on the day when the moon was in conjunction with the Aindra नक्षत्र (लेभे पुत्रं वरारोहा  … ऐन्द्रे चन्द्रसमायुक्ते) 1. 114. 3-4 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 123. 6: ऐन्द्रे ज्ये-ष्ठानक्षत्रे अष्टमे संवत्सरारम्भात्). B. Religious rites performed under this नक्षत्र: Nārada told Devakī (13. 63. 2-4) that if one gave to the Brāhmaṇas कालशाक with roots under Jyeṣṭhā one ob-tained prosperity wished for and cherished condition after death (कालशाकं तु विप्रे-भ्यो दत्त्वा मर्त्यः समूलकम् । ज्येष्ठा-याम् ऋद्धिम् इष्टां वै गतिम् इष्टां च विन्दति) 13. 63. 23; Yama told Śaśabindu (13. 89. 1) that if a man, with faith and self-control, offered a काम्य श्राद्ध under Jyeṣṭhā he got overlordship (आधिपत्यं व्रजेन् मर्त्यः) 13. 89. 9. C. Bad omens: Among the bad omens pointed out by Vyāsa to Dhṛtarāṣṭra there was one according to which the blazing black planet (i. e. Ketu), full of fire and smoke, had taken hold of Jyeṣṭhā, which was the bright Aindra नक्षत्र, and had remained there (श्यामो ग्रहः प्रज्वलितः सधूमः सहपावकः । ऐन्द्रं तेजस्वि नक्षत्रं ज्येष्ठाम् आक्र-म्य तिष्ठति) 6. 3. 15 (Nī., who reads श्वेतो ग्रहः in place of श्यामो ग्रहः, on Bom. Ed. 6. 3. 16 also explains it as Ketu: श्वेतो द्वितीय उपरहः केतुसंज्ञः ऐन्द्रं ज्येष्ठानक्षत्रम् इति योज्यम्; among the bad omens pointed out by Karṇa to Kṛṣṇa one was related to the retrograde movement of Mars in Jyeṣṭhā and his coveting Anurādhā as though thereby tranquilizing the Maitra Nakṣatrayoga (कृत्वा चाङ्गारको वक्रं ज्येष्ठायां मधुसूदन । अनुराधां प्रार्थयते मैत्रं संशमयन्न् इव ॥ ) 5. 141. 8 (For Nī.'s commentary on Bom. Ed. 5. 143. 9 See under Aṅgāraka, p. 229 above).
ज्येष्ठामूल: Jyeṣṭhāmūla m.: Name of the month Jyaiṣṭha. A. Religious rite performed in this month: Aṅgiras had told Bhīṣma that if a man or a woman passed the Jyeṣṭhāmūla month eating only once a day, he or she attained to prosperity which was incomparable and best 13. 109. 24 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 106. 25: ज्येष्थामूलं ज्येष्ठमासम्). B. Past event connected with this month: Jamadagni shot arrows at midday in the month Jyeṣṭhāmūla and asked his wife Reṇukā to fetch them (ततो मध्याह्नम् आरूढे ज्येष्ठामूले दिवाकरे । स सायकान् द्विजो विद्ध्वा रेणुकाम् इदम् अब्रवीत् ॥ गच्छानय विशालाक्षि शरान् एतान् धनु-श्च्युतान्) 13. 97. 9-10 (Unknown commen-tator: ज्येष्ठामूले ज्येष्ठमासे ज्येष्ठमा-सस्य मध्याह्ने अतितीक्ष्णः [दिवाकरः] इति सूचितम् । (cf. Cr. Edn. vol. 17, p. 1097, note on this stanza; Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 13. 95. 9: ज्येष्ठामूले दक्षिणावर्ते भ्र-ममाणे भचक्रे ज्येष्ठानां समसूत्रे पतितं रोहिणीनक्षत्रं तद् एव ज्येष्ठा-नां मूलम् । यथाश्रुतार्थग्रहणं तु न ज्येष्ठामूलस्थे ऽर्के हेमन्ते शिरःपाद-दाहस्यानवसरात् ॥ ).
जनकस्य: Janakasya kūpaḥ m.: Name (?) of a sacred well. Worshipped by gods (त्रिदशपूजित); by bathing there one obtained the Viṣṇuloka 3. 82. 95.
जम्बूनदी: Jambūnadī1 f.: Name of a river. The divine river Tripathagā (Gaṅgā), when it flowed down from the Brahmaloka, it was first established on the mountain Hiraṇya-śṛṅga; there it assumed seven forms (तत्र (i. e. on the Hiraṇyaśṛṅga 6. 7. 40) त्रिप-थगा देवी प्रथमं तु प्रतिष्ठिता । ब्रह्मलोकाद् अपक्रान्ता सप्तधा प्रति-पद्यते ॥ ) 6. 7. 44; Jambūnadī is one of these seven forms 6. 7. 45; all these seven Gaṅgās are described as heavenly (दिव्याः) and famous in the three worlds (त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुताः) 6. 7. 47.

Jambūnadī2 f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 29, 13; all the rivers listed here are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).

*Jambūnadī3 f.: Name of a fabulous river. It has its origin in the silvery juice (रजतसंनिभम् रसम्) of the ripe fruits which fall down, from the great Jambū tree, called Sudarśana, which is to the south of the Nīla and to the north of the Niṣadha moun-tain; the river flows around Meru keeping it to the right, and then goes to the Uttara Kurus; people drink that juice and then are not affected by oldage (तस्या जम्ब्वाः फलरसो नदी भूत्वा … । … तस्मिन् फलरसे पीते न जरा बाधते च तान्) 6. 8. 18, 22-24.
जम्बूमार्ग: Jambūmārga nt.: Name of a sacred place (प्रकीर्तितम् … जम्बूमार्गम् अथापि च 13. 151. 19). Described as frequented by gods, sages and manes (देवर्षिपितृसेवित) 3. 80. 60; one should go from Puṣkara to the Jambūmārga and from there to the Taṇḍulikāśrama 3. 80. 59, 62; one who visits this place gets the fruit of an Aśvamedha and secures for himself the Viṣṇuloka 3. 80. 60; if one lives there for five nights and eats only the sixth meal (in the evening of the third day) (षष्ठका-लक्षमी नरः) he will not meet with adver-sities and will obtain the best perfection (सिद्धिं प्राप्नोति चोत्तमाम्) 3. 80. 61; if one leads there a well disciplined life with a composed mind (संयतः सुसमाहितः) he would achieve perfection in a day (अहो-रात्रेण चैकेन सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति) 13. 26. 48; finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 19, 2.

Jambūmārga m.: Name of an आश्रम। Situated in the west 3. 87. 1; near the river Ketumālā 3. 87. 12; described as full of deer and birds (मृगद्विजगणायुत) 3. 87. 11; it was the आश्रम of ascetics whose souls were purified (जम्बूमार्गो महाराज ऋषीणाम् भावितात्मनाम् । आश्रमः) 3. 87. 11 [For Jambūmārga, name of a sacred place, see Vol. 1. 355].
जम्बूषण्ड: Jambūṣaṇḍa m.: Name (?) of a thicket of Jambū trees. Located in the Ketumāla Varṣa which is to the west of the mount Meru (मेरोस् तु पश्चिमे पार्श्वे केतुमालो महीपते । जम्बूषण्डश् च तत्रैव); described as very large and comparable with the Nandanavana (सुमहान् नन्दनोपमः) 6. 7. 29.
जयन्ती: Jayantī f.: Name of a river. Somatīrtha is situated on it 3. 81. 16.
जलधार: Jaladhāra m.: Name of a mountain of the Śākadvīpa. One of the seven mountains of the Śāka-dvīpa 6. 12. 15, 13; described as big (महा-गिरि) 6. 12. 15; all the seven mountains of this Dvīpa are described as adorned with jewels (मनिभूषिताः) and as mines of precious stones (रत्नाकराः) 6. 12. 13; Vāsava (Indra) always collects water in large quantity on this mountain (which explains the name of the mountain), and from that collection it rains in the rainy season (यत्र नित्यम् उपादत्ते वासवः परमं जलं । यतो वर्षं प्रभवति वर्षाकाले) 6. 12. 15.
जला: Jalā f.: Name of a river. Flowing near the river Yamunā (जलां  … यमुनां अभितो नदीम्); King Uśīnara offered a sacrifice there and surpassed Indra 3. 130. 17.
जातिमात्रह्रद: Jātimātrahrada m.: Name of a holy lake. Only by visiting (गमनाद् एव) this place one gets the reward of performing a hundred Agniṣṭoma sacrifices 3. 83. 34-35; and by bathing there one remembers one's past lives (जातिमात्रह्रदे स्नात्वा भवेज् जातिस्-मरो नरः) 3. 83. 36. [See Jātismara]
जातिस्मर: Jātismara nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। One who is pure and has a controlled mind, if he bathes (उपस्पृश्य) at this तीर्थ he is able to remember his past lives, and there is no doubt about this (this explains the name of the lake) (जातिस्मरत्वं प्रा-प्नोति स्नात्वा तत्र न संशयः) 3. 82. 110. [See Jātimātrahrada]
जाम्बूनद: Jāmbūnada nt.: Name of a lake. Located on the Uśīrabīja mountain in the north (यत्र जाम्बूनदं सरः); king Marutta performed there his sacrifice 5. 109. 20, 19; described as holy (पुण्य), clean (विमल), abounding in lotuses (कमला-कर), and related to the mountain Himavant (हैमवत) 5. 109. 21; the lake in person (the lake not named) waited on the brahma-nical sage Jīmūta (जीतूतस्यात्र विप्रर्षेर् उपतस्थे महात्मनः । साक्षात् … कमला-करः) 5. 109. 21.
जाम्बूनदपर्वत: Jāmbūnadaparvata m.: Name of a mountain. It belonged to Indra (इन्द्रस्य जाम्बू-नदपर्वताग्रे); Lomaśa heard the sound of the divine river Gaṅgā coming from the summit of the Jāmbūnada mountain 3. 140. 14.
जैमूत: Jaimūta nt.: Name (?) of a forest. The great sage Jīmūta chose to live in this forest after donating all his large wealth to the Brāhmaṇas (ब्राह्मणेषु च यत् कृत्-स्नं स्वन्तं कृत्वा धनं महत्); hence the forest was so called (वव्रे वनं महर्षिः स (i. e. जीमूतः) जैमूतं तद् वनं ततः) 5. 109. 22.
ज्येष्ठस्थान: Jyeṣṭhasthāna nt.: Name of a well. Sacred to Mahādeva; after going round the Koṭitīrtha (प्रदक्षिणम् उपावृत्य), one should go to the Jyesṭhasthāna, and from there proceed to Śṛṅgaverapura; by visiting Mahādeva (अभिगम्य महादेवम्) at this तीर्थ one shines like the moon; there is a famous well at this तीर्थ where the four oceans live (तत्र कूपो महाराज विश्रु-तो … । समुद्रास् तत्र चत्वारो निवसन्ति); by bathing (उपस्पृश्य) in this well and by making a प्रदक्षिणा round it a person who has controlled himself (नियतात्मा) becomes pure and attains the highest condition (पूतो गच्छेत परमां गतिम्) 3. 83. 59-61.
ज्येष्ठिल: Jyeṣṭhila nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Perhaps located in the Campakāraṇya (3. 82. 114); described as highly esteemed (परमसंमत) 3. 82. 115; sacred to Viśveśvara (Śiva); by fasting there for one night one got the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma; by taking there the दर्शन of Viśveśvara (तत्र विश्वेश्वरं दृष्ट्वा) together with the Devī (Umā) one attained the worlds of Mitra and Varuṇa (मित्रावरुणयोर् लोकान् आप्नोति) 3. 82. 115-116.
ज्योतिरथा: Jyotirathā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 25, 13; all the rivers listed here are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
ज्योतिरथी: Jyotirathī f.: Name of a river. One who is pure and while living at the confluence of the Śoṇa and the Jyotirathī satisfies manes and gods gets the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma (शोणस्य ज्योतिरथ्याश् च सं-गमे निवसञ् शुचिः । तर्पयित्वा पितॄन् देवान्) 3. 83. 8.
जनस्थान: Janasthāna nt.: Name of a region. A. Location: Situated in the Daṇḍa-kāraṇya 3. 147. 29; 3. 261. 40. B. Rāmā-yaṇa event: While Rāma lived in the Daṇḍakāraṇya he became the enemy of Khara who lived in Janasthāna (खरेण  … जनस्थाननिवासिना) 3. 261. 41; Rāvaṇa abducted Sītā from Janasthāna 3. 147. 30; in Janasthāna Rāma cut off the head of the demon (Khara or Dūṣaṇa ?) 9. 38. 10 (reference to 3. 261. 43). C. Holi-ness: According to the Tīrthavaṃśa narra-ted by Aṅgiras to Gautama, one who obser-ves fast and bathes in Janasthāna obtains royal glory (जनस्थाने … विगाह्य वै निरा-हारो राजलक्ष्मीं निगच्छति) 13. 26. 27.
जमदग्नेर्: *Jamadagner āśramaḥ m.: An आश्रम of Jamadagni. Jamadagni, after marrying Reṇukā, lived in his आश्रम and practised austerities with his wife 3. 116. 3; Reṇukā, when she went for bathing, saw king Citraratha and entertained longing for him; she then return-ed to the आश्रम 3. 116. 8; when Rāma returned to the आश्रम after collecting fruit (3. 116. 5), Jamadagni asked him to kill his mother 3. 116. 13-14; once Kārtavīrya, the king of Anūpa, arrived at the आश्रम (तम् आश्रमपदप्राप्तम्) and was received by Reṇukā; disregarding the respect shown to him, the king forcibly took away the calf of the cow whose milk was used for giving offerings (होमधेनु) and broke many big trees in the आश्रम 3. 116. 20-21; the sons of (Kārtavīrya) Arjuna attacked Jamadagni in the absence of Rāma from the आश्रम and killed him 3. 116. 25-26; Rāma returned to the आश्रम after collecting fuel (समित्-पाणिर् उपागच्छद् आश्रमं भृगुनन्दनः) 3. 116. 28; according to another account, as directed by the sea, Kārtavīrya went to the आश्रम of Jamadagni to find his match for a duel; he did things in the आश्रम which would not be liked by Rāma 14. 29. 8.
जारूथी: Jārūthī f. Name of a city. Kṛṣṇa defeated Āhuti, Krātha, Śiśu-pāla and his people, Bhīmasena, Śaibya, and Śatadhanvan at Jārūthī 3. 13. 27 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 12. 30: जारूथ्यां नगर्-याम्).
जगत्तुण्ड: Jagattuṇḍa m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people. Characterized as Janapada (एते जन-पदा … जगत्तुण्डाः) 6. 46. 50-51; on the second day of war, they were among those who were stationed at the left wing of the Krauñcāruṇavyūha (6. 46. 39) of the Pāṇḍavas 6. 46. 51.
जठर: Jaṭhara m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जन-पदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; जठराः कुक्कु-शाश् चैव 6. 10. 41.
जनक: Janaka m. (pl.): Designation of the family of Janaka. Aṣṭāvakra addressed king Janaka as the best in the family of Janakas (भो भो राजन् जनकानां वरिष्ठ) 3. 133. 16.
जम्बूद्वीप: Jambū̆dvīpa, Jambuparvata, Jambūkhaṇḍa  (m.): Name of a द्वीप (called Jambūkhaṇḍa 6. 12. 1, Jambuparvata 6. 12. 5). A. Location: One of the four द्वीपस् which lie on the four sides of mount Meru, the other three being Bhadrāśva, Ketumāla, and Uttara Kurus (मेरुः कनकपर्वतः । … तस्य पार्श्वे त्व् इमे द्वीपाश् चत्वारः संस्थिताः प्रभो । … जम्बूद्वीपश् च) 6. 7. 8, 11; Jambūdvīpa to the south of Meru 6. 12. 21-25; a great (Jambū) tree, which had become famous on account of Jambūdvīpa, stands in its middle (जम्पूद्वीपेन विख्यातस् तस्य मध्ये महाद्रुमः) 6. 12. 25. B. Name explained: The Dvīpa is named after the great, ancient Jambū tree, called Sudarśana, which stands on it (सुदर्शनो नाम महाञ् जम्बूवृक्षः सनातनः । … तस्य नाम्ना समाख्यातो जम्बूद्वीपः सनातनः) 6. 8. 18-19. C. Extent: Described by Saṃjaya for Dhṛtarāṣṭra 6. 12. 1; in extent it was a full eighteen thousand and six hundred योजनस् (अष्टादशसहस्राणि योजनानां विशां पते । षट्शतानि च पूर्णानि विष्कम्-भो जम्बुपर्वतः) ॥ 6. 12. 5 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 11. 5: विष्कम्भश् चतुर्दल-कमलाकारस्य जम्बूद्वीपस्य पत्रान्त-परिधिः तादृशविस्तार एव पिण्डप्रमाणम् अन्तर्भाव्य पर्वताकृतित्वाज् जम्बूपर्वत इत्य् उच्यते); its circular extent spread over many योजनस् (मण्डलं बहुयोजनम्) 6. 1. 9; the Śākadvīpa is double the size of Jambūdvīpa 6. 12. 9; its extent sometimes identified with Bhāratavarṣa (यावत् … जम्बू-द्वीपस्य मण्डलम् । तावद् एव समावृत्तं बलं … ) 6. 1. 8. D. Description: An-cient (सनातन) 6. 8. 18; the salty ocean which encircles it (सागरः परिम्ण्डलः) is double the extent of the Jambūdvīpa; the Jambūdvīpa is full of many Janapadas (नानाजनपदाकीर्ण) and is adorned with jewels and corals and by mountains which shine with many minerals (मणिविद्रुम-चित्रितः । नैकधातुविचित्रैश् च पर्वतैर् उपशोभितः); it is resorted to by Siddhas and Cāraṇas 6. 12. 6-7; (नानाजनपदा-युत) 12. 14. 21; 14. 87. 13; Krauñcadvīpa is similar to Jambūdvīpa 12. 14. 22. E. Characteristics: (1) Used as a measure of time: as much as it rains in the Jambū-dvīpa (i. e. the total number of drops of rain) for a thousand years, so long a person who fasts for a month eating only once on the last day lives in the Brahma-loka 13. 110. 121, 128; (2) Many kinds of jewels go from Jambūdvīpa to the other Dvīpas for the people living there (जम्बूद्वीपात् प्रवर्तन्ते रत्नानि विविधान्य् उत । द्वीपेषु तेषु सर्वेषु प्रजानां … ॥ 6. 13. 26. F. Epic events: (1) The army for the great war was drawn from the entire Jambūdvīpa (यावत् तपति सूर्यो हि जम्बूद्वीपस्य मण्डलम् । तावद् एव समावृत्तं बलम्) 6. 1. 8; (2) Drau-padī reminded Yudhiṣṭhira that he had formerly overpowered the entire Jambū-dvīpa 12. 14. 21; (3) In the Aśvamedha sacrifice of Yudhiṣṭhira, the entire Jambū-dvīpa had gathered (जम्बूद्वीपो हि सकलो  … अदृश्यतैकस्थो … ) 14. 87. 13. G. Past event: Nala became famous throughout Jambūdvīpa when he again became the king of Niṣadhas (प्रकाशतां यातो जम्बु-द्वीप) 3. 78. 4.
जागुड: Jāguḍa m. (pl.): Name of a people. Mentioned by Kṛṣṇa among those whom he saw at the Rājasūya of Yudhi-ṣṭhira and who acted as servers at meals (जागुडान् … आगतान् अहम् अद्राक्षं यज्ञे ते परिवेषकान्) 3. 48. 21-22.
जाङ्गल: Jāṅgala m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada (forest area as part of the Kuru country ?) and its residents. A. Location: Mentioned by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्धवं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (शाल्व-माद्रेयजाङ्गलाः) 6. 10. 37. B. Epic events: (1) Kṛṣṇa saw the inhabitants of Jāṅgala (here as opposed to पत्तन-वासिनः ?) attending the Rājasūya and act-ing as servers at meals (ये ते जाङ्गलवासि-नः … आगातान् अहम् अद्राक्षं यज्ञे ते परिवेषकान्) 3. 48. 19, 22; (2) Saṃjaya told Dhṛtarāṣṭra that the entire Kuru country along with the Jāṅgala had be-longed to him (कृत्सं राज्यं … कुरवस् ते सजाङ्गलाः) 5. 53. 6-7; [See Kuru-jāṅgala].
ज्येष्ठसामन्: Jyeṣṭhasāman nt.: Name of a Sāman. A. Referred to in some past events: (1) Upamanyu told Śakra that when he saw Śiva Mahādeva, he was being praised by all gods (13. 14. 146); Nārāyaṇa at that time praised Mahādeva by singing the स्तोत्र using Jyeṣṭhasāman (ज्येष्ठसाम्ना च देवेशं जगौ नारायणस् तदा) 13. 14. 147 [Editor's note, with a question mark, on the stanza, Vol. 17, p. 1060 Jyeṣṭhasāman = Bārhatasāman ?]; (2) In the Kṛtayuga the Sātvata Dharma was received by Brahman from Nārāyaṇa himself and was taught to the Barhiṣad sages; from them it went to a Brāhmaṇa called Jyeṣṭha who was versed in the Sāmaveda (सामवेदान्तगं द्विजम्); in this context it is said that god Hari observes the व्रत of Jyeṣṭhasāman (ज्येष्ठ-सामव्रतो हरिः) (i. e. Hari always uses Jyeṣṭhasāman while singing praises) 12. 336. 42. B. Its holiness: One who can sing a स्तोत्र using Jyeṣṭhasāman melody is included among those Brāhmaṇas who are considered to be पङ्क्तिपावन or पाङ्क्तेय (i. e. highly respectable, one who purifies those who sit in a line with him while tak-ing meals (पाङ्क्तेयांस् तु वक्ष्यामि ज्ञेयास् ते पङ्क्तिपावनाः । … छन्दोगो ज्येष्ठ-सामगः) 13. 90. 19-20.
